newsitem.title: FRANCE: Suspected ETA leader seized after chase in France.
newsitem.headline: Suspected ETA leader seized after chase in France.

text.p: French police captured the suspected number three leader of the Basque separatist guerrilla organisation ETA after a car chase in southwestern France, police said on Friday.

They said Jose Luis Urrusolo Sistiaga was stopped at a routine road check in Bordeaux on Thursday night. Armed with a handgun and carrying false papers, he drove off but was caught by police, they added. No shots were exchanged.

Urrusolo, among Spain's most wanted men, is suspected of being in charge of training commandos for ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom), which has killed around 800 people since 1968 in its violent campaign for an independent Basque state.
Urrusolo, alias Joseba and known to Spanish police as the "terrorist of a thousand faces", was born in the northern Spanish city of San Sebastian in 1957.
Police suspect of involvement in various killings in the early 1980s, including the murder of Banco Central managing director Ricardo Tejero on February 19, 1985.

Urrusolo was also alleged to have been involved in kidnapping of financier Diego Prado in 1983, blowing up the Telefonica building in Madrid in 1982 and a car bomb against a Civil Guard coach that killed an American jogger in Madrid.

After ETA's Madrid Command was broken up in January 1987, its leaders withdrew to southern France where they supposedly made up and trained a new group for Madrid, which was broken up in February 1988.
Urrusolo returned to Madrid and was subsequently accused of organising the kidnapping of businessman Emilian Revilla.

When a French roving command was broken up in 1990, he was alleged to have been put in charge of another similar group which organised a car bomb attack in September 1991 near Alicante that killed two police officers and a civilian.
Urrusolo is also thought by Spain to have been involved in three attacks in Madrid in October, 1991, in which a military officer died and three other people were injured.

In December 1991, Spanish police said they suspected Urrusolo was behind the murder of two police officers in Barcelona. They also attribute four fatal attacks to his command in Barcelona and Valencia in January, 1992.

Urrusolo fled before the Barcelona command was broken up and was thought to have returned to France, although in 1992 he left for Venezuela because of a clash with the then leader of the group, Francisco Mugica Garmendia "Pakito".
He later returned to France where he was suspected of having trained guerrillas.
Police also believe that Urrusulo has been involved in various criminal actions since then.
Cooperation between France and Spain has led to more than 200 arrests in the past decade and has hampered the rebels' ability to set up safe houses and arms factories in France.
The two nations recently increased joint meetings of anti- terrorist experts to exchange intelligence on the guerrillas.
Earlier this week, France handed over a former ETA leader, Josu Arkauz Arana, to Spanish police after he completed a prison sentence in France. He had been in jail in France since 1991.
